newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice mixed, Philippines drought watched.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice mixed, Philippines drought watched.

text.p: Thai rice was mixed this week as the market watched to see how the drought developed in the Philippines, anticipating the country might need to buy rice soon, trade sources said on Thursday.
Overall, fresh demand was thin as buyers were sidelined by high prices induced by tight supplies. However, the upside was limited by the weakening baht, they said.
"There are some enquiries. But actual deals were almost non-existent this week as prices remain high," said a Bangkok trader.
The market is closely watching the drought effect in the Philippines and the floods in China's southern Guandong province.
The Philippines could import as much as 350,000 tonnes of rice in case of a domestic production shortfall due to threats of a drought, trade sources said.
A senior official in Manila said a decision on whether to import would depend on the volume of rice harvests next month.
At the same time, floods in Guangdong were seen cutting the province's rice output substantially.

However, Thailand might not fully benefit from the woes of China and the Philippines, although they were both major Thai rice buyers, because the country was suffering its own dry spell, traders said.
The unseasonably late rainy season forced farmers in many areas to delay planting, causing short-term tight supplies.
"We believe the Philippines will need to buy soon. But they might not find our prices very attractive," said one exporter.
The rice prices were mixed this week. The benchmark 100 percent B grade was steady to lower while the 100 percent fragrant rice continue to soar.
Thai parboiled rice, popular among African consumers, also firmed to $348-$360 per tonne FOB Bangkok from around $330 last week, traders said.
Broken rice also firmed due to shortages of corn. Feedmills turned to broken rice as a substitute for corn, forcing the prices up to around $220 per tonne.
At the port, five vessels were loading 39,800 tonnes of rice for delivery to Brunei and Malaysia, Nigeria and other African countries.
Thailand has exported up to 2.69 million tonnes of rice between January 1 and July 29.
